title: Ivo and the Alibi
premise: True-crime podcaster Vesper Thackeray receives a retainer from a dying man, Ivo Marchetti, who insists he will be murdered within the year and wants her to prove it before the statute of limitations on his family's original crime expires. As Vesper investigates the Thackeray-adjacent inheritance that binds Ivo to four estranged heirs, she discovers the 'future murder' is a rehearsed alibi — a killing already planned and pre-forgiven by everyone but its victim. When Ivo dies on schedule, Vesper must trap the killer using the killer's own obsession with the case file, exposing that the murderer is the one heir who was never in the will: her client's long-lost daughter, whom Vesper has unknowingly befriended. In the end, loyalty to the dead forces Vesper to choose truth over the found family she built chasing the story.
about_author: Oscar Winterbourne is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. They live on the Cornish coast, where they write mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Vesper Thackeray, mid-recording on her coldest-case episode, meets Ivo Marchetti, an elderly notary who pays a year's fee upfront to have her prove his murder hasn't happened yet. His calm terrifies her more than fear would. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: uneasy fascination — the hook of a case that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: A Will Without a Grave
chapters.summary: Ivo shows Vesper a sealed testament naming four heirs and one deliberate omission, insisting the omission is the motive for a killing scheduled like an appointment. Vesper interviews him formally; he answers questions she hasn't asked. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Four Heirs, One Table
chapters.summary: Vesper attends the annual Marchetti family dinner under cover as Ivo's archivist, meeting heirs Marcus, Odile, Tobias, and the warm, sharp innkeeper Renata — who claims no blood tie to Ivo at all. Old grievances surface over dessert. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the seduction of found family, and its falseness.

chapters.title: Cold Open
chapters.summary: Researching the family's buried history, Vesper finds the 1974 death of Ivo's brother, ruled accidental, statute long expired but records suspiciously complete — too complete, as if curated. Someone has been editing the file for fifty years. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into paranoia.

chapters.title: What Ivo Knows
chapters.summary: Confronted, Ivo admits he witnessed something in 1974 and built his life around protecting the guilty — including, perhaps, himself. He refuses names but gives Vesper a key to a deposit box. POV: alternating Vesper and Ivo's dictated memoir tapes. Emotional beat: guilt as a lifelong tenant.

chapters.title: The Deposit Box
chapters.summary: Inside the box: the original coroner's photo, a second will, and a page torn from a ledger listing payments made annually to someone coded only as 'R.' Vesper photographs everything, then finds her hotel room searched. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: violation — the case now knows her back.

chapters.title: Renata's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Seeking warmth, Vesper spends an evening at Renata's inn; the conversation drifts toward mothers, belonging, and what we owe the families we choose. Vesper leaves lighter than she's felt in years — then realizes Renata asked nothing about herself, and answered everything. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: intimacy as misdirection.

chapters.title: Odile's Version
chapters.summary: Heir Odile, brittle and precise, tells Vesper the family's official story of 1974 — and lets slip that Ivo has been 'saying goodbye' for months, settling debts, returning objects. The murder has a countdown, and Ivo set it. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: horror at realizing the victim is complicit.

chapters.title: Tobias Runs
chapters.summary: When Vesper presses Tobias about the ledger's 'R,' he panics and flees town, leaving behind a train ticket dated the week after Ivo's predicted death. Is he fleeing guilt or planning escape? POV: Vesper, with a brief interlude from Tobias's voicemails. Emotional beat: suspicion narrowing, unfairly.

chapters.title: Marcus and the Money
chapters.summary: Marcus, the eldest heir, is drowning in debt and stands to lose everything unless the estate settles soon — motive with a deadline. But his alibi for the predicted date is ironclad, almost rehearsed. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: frustration as every suspect fits too neatly.

chapters.title: The File That Reads You
chapters.summary: Vesper maps the doctored case file against her own investigation and realizes the edits mirror her own discoveries step by step — someone inside her circle knows exactly what she knows, and when. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: isolation; the podcaster becomes the surveilled.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Date Arrives
chapters.summary: The predicted night passes. Ivo is alive, serene, almost disappointed. He thanks Vesper — and fires her, claiming the danger has passed. She doesn't believe it for a second. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: false relief, the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Fired, Not Finished
chapters.summary: Off the clock, Vesper digs into 'R' and finds the payments funded a child's upbringing abroad — Ivo's daughter, born in secret, erased from the will by his own hand. The omitted heir exists. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grief for a girl punished before she could sin.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Records lead Vesper to a name: Rhea. Adopted out in 1975, returned quietly as an adult, employed — she realizes with a chill — at the county archive where the case file lives. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the puzzle clicking together with terrible elegance.

chapters.title: Rhea
chapters.summary: Vesper meets Rhea, archivist, gentle, guarded — and recognizes the woman she's been calling a friend at Renata's inn under another name. Rhea denies nothing and admits nothing. POV: dual — Vesper's confrontation intercut with Rhea's quiet preparations. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: Why Ivo Hired Her
chapters.summary: Decoding Ivo's memoir tapes, Veper understands: he hired a witness, not an investigator. He wanted his daughter's crime proven before the statute closed so she couldn't inherit through his death — his final act of protection and punishment at once. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: fury at a man who scripted his own murder.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: With days left before the old case legally closes — sealing the evidence forever — Vesper races to authenticate the deposit-box documents while Rhea methodically retrieves and destroys copies. Each woman needs the same paper for opposite reasons. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: a duel conducted in silence.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Vesper locates the second will, which restores Rhea's inheritance contingent on one condition: that she never harm Ivo. Whoever holds it controls everything. Rhea asks Vesper, plainly, to let it burn. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: temptation — mercy dressed as destruction.

chapters.title: Climax: The Archive After Hours
chapters.summary: Vesper baits Rhea with a forged copy of the will, trapping her in the archive overnight among the very files she curated. Confronted with the 1974 truth — Ivo caused his brother's death, and the payments were hush money to raise the orphaned child — Rhea breaks. POV: both, converging. Emotional beat: the collision of loyalty and truth.

chapters.title: Confession, Recorded
chapters.summary: Rhea confesses not to murder but to intent — the plan, the date, the rehearsed alibi — while Vesper records, hating every second. Ivo arrives, having followed them, and forgives her aloud, which wounds worse than accusation. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: compassion as the sharpest blade.

chapters.title: Ivo's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Before charges can be weighed, Ivo dies naturally — on no one's schedule — leaving the estate split between the heirs and a trust funding cold-case investigations in Vesper's name. Rhea, spared prosecution for an uncommitted crime, must live with the version of herself she met in the archive. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Cold Open, Warm Close
chapters.summary: Months later, Vesper releases the season finale, telling everything except Rhea's name — her first act of loyal silence, and possibly her last. Rhea writes once: thank you, and don't ever again. Vesper opens a new case file. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: found family, forgiven but never forgotten.
